e: Greece repatriates the remains of Samuel of Bulgaria, which were previously stored in Thessaloniki, to Sofia.
A drone that originated from Romania explodes near a section of the Trans-Balkan pipeline in the vicinity of the Kardam border crossing.
The National Assembly approves the stationing of an American aerial refueling tanker at Bezmer Air Base.
The Monument to Vasil Levski in Targovishte is officially opened.
The Radev government announces that it would stop supplying weapons to Ukraine.
Bulgaria's Dara wins Eurovision 2026 in Austria with the single "Bangaranga", making her the first contestant from Bulgaria to win the Eurovision Song Contest.
Rumen Radev is formally elected as prime minister by the National Assembly.
President Iotova nominates Andrey Gyurov, the deputy governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, as caretaker prime minister. He is formally appointed the next day.
Iliana Iotova becomes the first female president of Bulgaria following Rumen Radev's resignation.
President Rumen Radev announces his resignation effective 23 January.
